subject: Civic Education
competence: Appreciates the nature of multicultural societies and demonstrates the importance of cooperative living through mutual trust and collective conscience.
lesson: Explains with examples that Sri Lanka as a multicultural society: Voices of Harmony: Interactive Roleplay on Cooperative Living
unique_learning_outcome: Explains with examples that Sri Lanka as a multicultural society.
Expresses views appreciating the importance of living cooperatively as a member of a multicultural society.
the_entrance: The teacher writes 'Village Harmony Committee Meeting' on the chalkboard and launches a 5-minute motivational hook by presenting a short real-world scenario of a Sri Lankan village planning a common Avurudu and Thai Pongal joint celebration. The teacher prompts students to reflect on how different cultural traditions enrich our community life. Students enthusiastically respond by sharing their own experiences of participating in neighborhood religious festivals, quickly forming their 6 collaborative teams of 5 members with designated group roles (Leader, Scribe, Timekeeper, Spokesperson, Civic Investigator) to prepare for the committee roleplay.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher acts as a facilitator, circulating among the 6 groups to distribute scenario task cards detailing a local village water-management or festival-planning dilemma involving diverse ethnic residents. The teacher guides students in fair role distribution and asks probing questions such as, 'How can our village committee ensure every religious group's customs are respected in this plan?'
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students work collaboratively in their assigned groups of 5 to read their scenario card and allocate roles representing diverse village elders, farmers, and youth leaders. The Scribe records the initial talking points while the Civic Investigator checks facts against textbook definitions of multicultural coexistence, drafting a 2-minute dialogue outline.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_method: Neighborhood Committee Scripting and Character Allocation
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chart Paper, Marker Pens, Student Notebooks, Role Character Cards

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher observes team rehearsals, manages strict time pacing, and moderates the rapid presentation of the 2-minute roleplay enactments from each team. The teacher scaffolds student reflections by asking the class to identify specific instances of mutual trust and cooperative problem-solving demonstrated during the performances.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Group Spokespersons present their dramatized neighborhood committee solutions to the class, illustrating how different language speakers and custom followers resolve community disputes cooperatively. Following the enactments, all students collaboratively write a concise 3-sentence summary in their notebooks highlighting why minimizing conflicts through mutual respect builds sustainable peace in Sri Lanka.

summary: In this 2-minute synthesis, students collectively conclude that Sri Lanka's multicultural fabric—encompassing diverse languages, religions, and customs—requires active mutual trust, collective conscience, and daily cooperation to minimize conflicts and foster national development.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative evaluation is conducted through observation of active group participation, the realism and depth of the roleplay dialogue regarding multicultural cooperation, and the accuracy of the 3-sentence notebook summaries evaluated against NIE curriculum standards.
post_activity: Within a 5-minute in-class window, students engage in a creative 'Harmony Mosaic Chain' activity. Each student is given a small colored paper slip to quickly write one specific example of how Sri Lankan multiculturalism is visible in their daily life (e.g., sharing food during Vesak and Ramadan). Students rapidly link their paper slips together into a continuous classroom paper chain hung across the chalkboard, while the teacher provides instant verbal praise and formative feedback on the diversity of cultural examples contributed.
selected_activity:
Activity: Voices of Harmony: Interactive Roleplay on Cooperative Living
Approach: Students enact a short neighborhood committee meeting in a Sri Lankan village discussing how to organize a community event that welcomes all ethnic and religious groups. They explore the practical importance of mutual respect and cooperation.
Student task: Each group scripts and performs a 2-minute roleplay scenario demonstrating how neighbors from diverse backgrounds cooperate to solve a common community challenge.
Teacher facilitation: Sets the scenario context on the chalkboard, guides groups in distributing character roles fairly, monitors rehearsal time limits, and facilitates brief plenary reflections.
Expected output: A short dramatized enactment and a written 3-sentence summary in notebooks highlighting the value of cooperative multicultural living.
Grouping: 6 teams (6 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer
